messages.content: What are the most common chords in a pop song?

function.name: music_theory_primary_triads
function.description: Get the primary triads for a given key signature. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

key_signature.description: The key signature to calculate the primary triads for.

include_inversions.description: Whether or not to include inversions in the returned triads.

message.content:
In most pop songs the harmonic palette is pretty small.  
The chords that show up most often are the **primary triads** of the key:

| Function | Roman numeral | Example in C major |
|----------|---------------|--------------------|
| Tonic    | I             | C major            |
| Subdominant | IV         | F major            |
| Dominant | V             | G major            |
| Relative minor | vi     | A minor            |
| Super‑tonic | ii          | D minor            |
| Mediant | iii            | E minor            |

A very common progression that uses four of those is **I–V–vi–IV** (e.g., C–G–Am–F in C major).  
Other frequent patterns involve the ii–V–I turnaround or the vi–IV–I–V sequence.  

So, if you’re looking for the “most common chords” in pop, focus on I, IV, V, vi, ii, and iii – especially the I–V–vi–IV loop.
